I've read that you should plant in a square hole to discourage the roots from going in circles instead of outward. Also to make the edges rough, not smooth, and use a tool to poke random holes into the sides of the hole to give the roots easier pathways outward.

Don't fertilize as it can send the plant into shock. Water deeply every other day or two, depending on your climate's dryness, is preferable to daily light watering. Don't allow it to set fruit this year as you want it to focus on making roots instead. If you have anything at all that might like to munch on it, get a protector to put around the base. If you have dwarf trees, space them 15' from other trees. Full size should be 20'. This probably varies depending on your particular Apple variety so look it up and honor it.

Make sure that you have a compatible pollinator variety to go with it, if it's not self pollinating. Often times even self pollinating produce far better if you get another variety. Consider grafting a different variety to the one you have if you're short on space.
